encounters.chiefComplaint: Quarterly diabetes and renal function follow-up with mild ankle edema
encounters.rawClinicalNotes: Patient presents for 3-month diabetes follow-up. Takes metformin 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 20 mg daily consistently. Reports mild bilateral ankle swelling over 2 weeks without orthopnea or chest pain. Exam: BP 138/84, HR 76, 1+ pitting pedal edema bilaterally, lungs clear. Labs: HbA1c 8.1%, eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73m2, urine ACR 145 mg/g. Add empagliflozin 10 mg daily for cardiorenal protection.
encounters.diagnosisDetails: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic stage 3a CKD; controlled essential hypertension
encounters.treatmentPlan: Continue metformin and lisinopril; start empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; repeat BMP and HbA1c in 3 months
encounters.labResultsText: HbA1c: 8.1% (H) | eGFR: 48 mL/min/1.73m2 (L) | Urine ACR: 145 mg/g (H) | K+: 4.4 mEq/L

uploadedDocuments.extractedSummary: HbA1c 8.1%, eGFR 48, Urine ACR 145 mg/g indicating stage 3a CKD.

soapNote.subjective: 64-year-old male presents for scheduled 3-month diabetes follow-up. Reports consistent adherence to metformin 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Endorses mild bilateral ankle swelling for 2 weeks. Denies chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, or orthopnea.
soapNote.objective: BP 138/84 mmHg, HR 76 bpm. Cardiovascular: regular rate and rhythm without murmurs. Pulmonary: lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema bilaterally at ankles. Labs: HbA1c 8.1%, eGFR 48 mL/min/1.73m2, Urine ACR 145 mg/g, Potassium 4.4 mEq/L.
soapNote.assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease (stage 3a, eGFR 48, elevated urine ACR 145 mg/g).
2. Essential hypertension, adequately controlled on lisinopril.
soapNote.plan:
1. Initiate empagliflozin 10 mg PO once daily for glycemic control and nephroprotection.
2. Continue metformin 1000 mg BID and lisinopril 20 mg daily.
3. Order repeat basic metabolic panel and HbA1c in 3 months.
4. Counsel patient to monitor ankle swelling and report sudden weight gain or dyspnea.

encounters.labResultsText: CXR preliminary: focal pulmonary infiltrate (laterality pending final radiology read). WBC not ordered.

encounters.chiefComplaint: Routine atrial fibrillation rate control check and left knee pain flare
encounters.rawClinicalNotes: 71yo female with paroxysmal AFib on apixaban 5 mg BID and metoprolol 50 mg. Feels well, no palpitations or bleeding. Also notes worsening left knee stiffness over 3 weeks. BP 126/72, HR 66 regular. Penicillin allergy (anaphylaxis) verified. Avoid NSAIDs due to apixaban + prior GI sensitivity; recommend topical diclofenac gel or acetaminophen.
encounters.diagnosisDetails: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; primary osteoarthritis of left knee
encounters.treatmentPlan: Continue apixaban 5 mg BID and metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; initiate topical diclofenac 1% gel to left knee TID
encounters.labResultsText: Serum creatinine: 0.92 mg/dL | eGFR: 64 mL/min | Hemoglobin: 12.8 g/dL

soapNote.subjective: 71-year-old female presents for routine paroxysmal atrial fibrillation review. Denies palpitations, syncope, epistaxis, or melena. Reports 3 weeks of worsening left knee stiffness and aching.
soapNote.objective: BP 126/72 mmHg, HR 66 bpm regular, SpO2 98% on room air. Labs: Serum creatinine 0.92 mg/dL, eGFR 64 mL/min, Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL.
soapNote.assessment:
1. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, rate-controlled and stable on apixaban and metoprolol.
2. Unilateral primary osteoarthritis, left knee.
soapNote.plan:
1. Continue apixaban 5 mg PO BID (renal function stable, Cr 0.92) and metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
2. Prescribe topical diclofenac 1% gel to left knee TID; counsel to avoid oral NSAIDs due to bleeding risk with anticoagulation.
3. Routine follow-up in 6 months.

encounters.chiefComplaint: Acute right knee pain and mechanical locking 5 days post soccer injury
encounters.rawClinicalNotes: 39yo male with right knee pain and locking after twisting injury 5 days ago. Exam: joint effusion, medial joint line tenderness, positive McMurray test. MRI right knee confirms bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus, initial encounter. Plan knee arthroscopy consult and naproxen? Wait—patient has ibuprofen gastric upset allergy! Needs GI-safe analgesia review.
encounters.diagnosisDetails: Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus, right knee, initial encounter
encounters.treatmentPlan: Orthopedic arthroscopy scheduling; knee immobilizer; acetaminophen 650 mg q6h PRN (avoid oral NSAIDs given ibuprofen intolerance)
encounters.labResultsText: MRI Right Knee: Displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus; ACL/PCL intact.

soapNote.subjective: 39-year-old male presents 5 days after acute twisting injury of right knee during soccer with persistent medial knee pain and mechanical locking. Documented gastric upset with ibuprofen.
soapNote.objective: Right knee exam: mild joint effusion, medial joint line tenderness, positive McMurray maneuver. MRI right knee confirms bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus with intact cruciate ligaments.
soapNote.assessment: Acute bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus, right knee, initial encounter.
soapNote.plan:
1. Refer to orthopedic surgery for arthroscopic meniscal repair evaluation.
2. Place right knee in immobilizer and advise protected weight-bearing.
3. Recommend acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain; avoid ibuprofen/NSAIDs due to prior gastric intolerance.
